articles.title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
articles.summary: NBA News: Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindnessOn Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct. 10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I try to be the connector": Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry open up about their equal partnership in charity work
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have always been a team even though their marriage has been surrounded by a number of negative rumors throug.
articles.body: Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have always been a team even though their marriage has been surrounded by a number of negative rumors throughout the last decade. Despite the negative drama, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have remained united in all their efforts.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry explain how the two divide their work equally when it comes to their charityA few weeks ago, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry opened up about her work and department in their foundation, Eat. Play. Live, as she said, “I feel like I’m the big-ideas girl. I always have big, loud ideas that I want to accomplish now — or yesterday. The hardest thing for me, personally, has been reeling back a bit to come to the understanding that baby steps are important.”The four time NBA champion Stephen Curry also opened up about his area of work as he added, “I try to be the connector, especially when we’re reaching out to our network. We’re building a family, in a sense, of people who, again, believe in our mission and want to commit time and resources, whether that be financial or otherwise.”The Golden State Warriors’ star player continued, “When I’m on the court, I want people to enjoy the way that I played…I want them to feel something and be inspired to achieve greatness in whatever they decide to do. Family-wise, we want to have a cohort of hopefully thousands of kids whose lives have been impacted because of the work that we’ve done. We don’t need a parade for that. It’s who we are.”Both the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have remained dedicated towards building their foundation, Eat. Learn and Play, throughout the last decade.Eat. Learn and Play has actively worked for underprivileged children and families in Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s hometown, Oakland.Throughout the last decade, the team has actively worked for over 10,000 children and has looked after their food and provided quality education.Both Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have handled their busy professional and personal lives while they have actively worked towards the children in Oakland.Stephen Curry focuses on recovery amid concerns over his fitness ahead of the new seasonAhead of the new season, there have been many concerns about Stephen Curry’s fitness after he ended up sustaining a patellofemoral pain syndrome (runner's knee) and bone bruising in his right knee which kept him out of court for two months.Even though the NBA legend could come back for his team, Stephen Curry has kept his full focus on complete recovery during the offseason.With the Golden State Warriors scheduled to play a demanding season, many remain stressed about him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook after spending $18,000 an hour flight for teammates: See Photos
articles.summary: NBA News: Luka Doncic has made his first major statement as the undisputed face of the Los Angeles Lakers. With LeBron James gone after joining the Philadelphia.
articles.body: Luka Doncic has made his first major statement as the undisputed face of the Los Angeles Lakers. With LeBron James gone after joining the Philadelphia 76ers, Doncic brought the Lakers to Slovenia for a four-day minicamp designed to build chemistry before his first full season as the franchise's centerpiece. He welcomed his teammates with dinner, workouts, pickup games, golf and time exploring Ljubljana, turning an offseason trip into an early test of his leadership.Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook in LeBron James-less eraThe itinerary mixed basketball with leisure. The players worked out, played pickup games, visited Lake Bled for fishing, played golf and explored Ljubljana. Dinner at Doncic's favorite restaurant was also part of the trip.Doncic's Instagram Story captured the start of the gathering with a simple caption: “First supper,” Doncic wrote.The Lakers enter the 2026-27 season with Doncic at the center of everything. James' departure ended a defining chapter in Los Angeles, while Doncic's first full season as the team's unquestioned leader begins with a roster built around his offensive game.Doncic's production gives the Lakers plenty to build on. He led the league with 33.5 points per game in 2025-26 while averaging 8.3 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 1.6 steals. He shot 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from 3-point range.Los Angeles also made significant moves around him. The Lakers retained Austin Reaves on a four-year, $185 million contract and acquired Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz through a sign-and-trade. Kessler received a four-year, $130 million deal, while the Lakers also sent two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the transaction.Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Kevon Looney, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams were among the other additions. It appears that the Lakers are constructing a roster intended to maximize Doncic's strengths.Luka Doncic reportedly spent $18,000 an hour for teammatesThe trip also came with a remarkable price tag. Doncic reportedly chartered a Bombardier Global 8000 for 14 Lakers players, with the 13-hour flight costing at least $18,000 per hour. The 26-hour round trip is expected to cost roughly $500,000, according to Slovenian outlet 24ur.com, with Doncic covering the expense.Doncic's leadership has not been limited to roster decisions. The Slovenia trip gave him a chance to create the kind of shared experience that can be difficult to manufacture during an NBA season.The 14 players reportedly traveled aboard a luxurious Bombardier Global 8000. Images from the flight showed a lounge area, individual bedrooms, beds, couches, recliners and televisions. After arriving, Doncic met his teammates alongside his daughter, Gabriela.The Lakers need their new hierarchy to work on the court, but Doncic also needs to establish himself inside a locker room that previously revolved around James.The Lakers are building the roster around DoncicThis is not Doncic's first attempt at bringing his teammates together. He organized a Porsche Driving Experience for the Lakers in October 2025, shortly after joining the organization.This minicamp carries more weight. James is no longer there, and Doncic now enters the season without another established superstar occupying the franchise's leadership role.The Lakers are also dealing with significant organizational change. Mark Walter's $12.5 billion purchase of the team and the Buss family's dispute over its remaining stakes have added another layer of uncertainty around the franchise.Doncic has so far handled that backdrop while remaining focused on basketball. The Slovenia minicamp gives him an opportunity to set the tone before training camp and the regular season arrive.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kevin Durant’s mother Wanda Durant remains his biggest support system as the Rockets' star shares an emotional moment with her
articles.summary: Kevin Durant, the Houston Rockets’ star player, has always been public about how his mother, Wanda Durant, has supported him through all the challenging
articles.body: Kevin Durant, the Houston Rockets’ star player, has always been public about how his mother, Wanda Durant, has supported him through all the challenging days in his personal and professional life. As Kevin Durant’s team defeated the Washington Wizards 147–119 in Washington, D.C., his moment with his mother has made many emotional.Kevin Durant makes his mother, Wanda Durant, a priority as the Houston Rockets defeat the Washington WizardsA few hours ago, a clip posted on social media by the NBA shows the 38 year old NBA icon Kevin Durant seeking his mother Wanda Durant, after the game as he shared a warm hug with her.The Houston Rockets’ legend Kevin Durant was also spotted showing his mother around the court as Kevin Durant’s mother, Wanda Durant, seemed ecstatic with her son’s achievements on the court.The heartwarming moment has made many emotional as this was not the first time that Kevin Durant’s mother, Wanda Durant, showed up to be by his side.Over the last two decades, Kevin Durant’s mother Wanda Durant has been one of strongest pillars of strength and support to him.Kevin Durant’s mother, Wanda Durant, has always motivated him to do better in his lifeBack in 2017, in an appearance on Good Morning America, Kevin Durant’s mother Wanda Durant opened up about her son leading the Golden State Warriors to win the NBA championship.Kevin Durant’s mother Wanda Durant said, "I felt fulfilled as a mom…When he gave the speech and he talked about me in the speech ... I felt like he got, he understood why I was the type of mother that I was. There were several times I wanted to quit, but the look in their eyes was what kept me going ... no matter how hard it was I just couldn't be a quitter for them,"Kevin Durant’s mother Wanda Durant added, "On the court I was very demanding in practice and workouts. The coach would say 'Kevin do 25 push-ups,' and I would come in with my flippin attitude and say 'do 250,'" Durant said. "I just taught him how to go beyond what was required and dig deeper."Kevin Durant’s mother Wanda Durant also reflected on how she brought up her children as she said, "Being engaged with your children helps you identify characteristics for certain professions or hobbies or interests. It just happened to be basketball for us. But just being able to identify the artistic characteristics in your child, the academic prowess and the athletic ability if you're there and present."For now, all eyes remain on Kevin Durant as he has recorded a pretty impressive performance on the court. As per reports, through his first 14 games, the 38 year old forward is averaging 21.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 1.1 blocks in 33.9 minutes per game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lakers Must Pursue Naz Reid Trade To Give Luka Chance at Championship amid Latest NBA Rumors
articles.summary: If the Los Angeles Lakers get involved with the upcoming iteration of NBA trade season, they need to find ways of stretching their trade budget.
articles.body:
If the Los Angeles Lakers get involved with the upcoming iteration of NBA trade season, they need to find ways of stretching their trade budget.

They haven't exhausted their asset collection, but they're pretty close after the costly sign-and-trade for Walker Kessler this summer. So, in a perfect world, they'd find a reasonably priced pickup capable of checking multiple boxes.

Perhaps this single-stone-for-multiple-birds pursuit could steer them toward Charlotte Hornets combo big Naz Reid, who has a "very high" chance of getting traded, per The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski . Or rather, that should probably say steer them back toward Reid, since they "called" on his availability over the offseason, per Dan Woike of The Athletic.

If the Lakers can afford a Reid trade, that would be worth the piggy bank-bursting splurge to get him.

They probably need the Hornets to be big fans of Cameron Carr or Adou Thiero (or both) for a trade to materialize, but that feels possible if Charlotte opts to lean harder into a youth movement around Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel. Especially with things off to a less-than-ideal start for Reid and for the Hornets as a whole (4-9 with a minus-11.1 net rating , per NBA.com).

In a better basketball situation, though, Reid could flourish.

The 6'9", 264-pounder pairs perimeter finesse with paint force. What that means is he could be the stretchy scoring presence they need at the 4 spot while also shoring up that problematic backup big man role.

He was a supersub (and one-time Sixth Man of the Year) on some high-level Minnesota Timberwolves teams. Reid might be even better positioned to flourish with the Lakers, as they feature even more creation and playmaking with the backcourt combo of Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves.

Reid can be an all-purpose screen-setter, since he can shred nets from distance or explode to (and above) the rim off of hard rolls. He can find open teammates on quick, simple, gear-turning passes. He can rebound and protect the paint.

In short, he has that coveted across-the-board skill set that every team seeks in its supporting cast.

Trade cost is a consideration, obviously, but it's hard to imagine Reid's would be overwhelming. He is shooting just 39.9 percent from the field and has never been a full-time starter prior to this season.

He is a rock-solid contributor, but he might be overpaid in the second season of a five-year, $125 million pact. The Lakers should be conscious of that, but as long as that gets factored into his trade price, that's probably something they could stomach.

They just have to believe the on-court upgrade is worth it. Given the obvious overlap between his skills and their wish list, that shouldn't be the hardest sell.

And they should have some leverage in these talks. As proud owners of a red-hot 12-2 record, they don't need Reid on this roster. One could argue they shouldn't feel the need to look outside the organization for any kind of help.

Remember, though, their aim goes way beyond first-month domination. If they want to convert this sizzling start into sustained success come playoff time, then their front office needs to be nitpicky while holding this roster to the highest possible standard.

Through those elevated expectations, L.A. probably can sense a few needs. Like more scoring from the forward spots. And a lot more reliability and impact out of its backup center.

Reid is capable of scratching both itches. In fact, he might be the most capable of doing so among all trade candidates they could realistically afford.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo Talks GTA 6-Inspired NBA 2K27 Cover, Rating, Giannis, Heat and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Miami Heat star center Bam Adebayo has made no secret of how much he was influenced by the late Kobe Bryant, and he's following in his idol's footsteps once again.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star center Bam Adebayo has made no secret of how much he was influenced by the late Kobe Bryant, and he's following in his idol's footsteps once again.

After surpassing Bryant's iconic 81-point game with an 83-point performance last season, Adebayo joined the Black Mamba and many other greats as the cover star of the NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition, a new collaboration with Rockstar Games ahead of Thursday's highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

"Man, I grew up playing this game wholeheartedly. Just to be part of 2K, I got that chance, but also now I get to see myself on a cover. You know, because a lot of our idols were on the cover of 2K, like mine was Kobe," Adebayo told Bleacher Report. "To see Kobe on the front of a cover was like, 'Yo, this is his game.' So, to have that moment to be a part of it and to be the cover is just, it's surreal."

The NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition is available digitally from Nov. 27 through Jan. 15 across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC via Steam. The extended, seven-week Season 3 will include fresh content such as a brand-new Vice City-inspired park in The City, Vice City-themed rewards and apparel, and more.

The Heat will be celebrating the release of Grand Theft Auto VI in Wednesday's home game against the Milwaukee Bucks, dubbed "A Night in Vice City." Adebayo and his teammates will be wearing special-edition Nike x Cactus Jack uniforms that can now be found in NBA 2K27.

As a nine-year veteran who has spent his entire career in Miami, Adebayo was excited to see South Beach under the spotlight.

"I take no credit, obviously, because it's Miami, but like, if you lived in this city, you understand how great this city really is," he said. "To be a part of Vice City and to know the history, you never really have a bad day, besides the rain. Every once in a while, we get some rain, but to be in the middle of January and it's 80 degrees, you can't put it into words. There's always something to do here, it's just an active city."

After being revealed as NBA 2K's newest cover star, Adebayo joked that he has to do some lobbying to get his 87 overall rating bumped up. While he doesn't have much time for video games during the NBA season, he said he plans to hone his skills so he can hold his own against the youngsters in the Heat locker room.

"I don't know, man. I guess just have a conversation with Ronnie at this point. I'll be like, man, you can give me at least a 90," he said with a laugh. "But it is what it is, I don't get too mad about it. To me, for what the young kids say, I'm actually nice in 2K. My build, apparently I got the best build, low-key. But the game is too advanced now. So, I play when I can, but the shot meter all quick and everything. Now I'm like, 'Hold on, man!'"

Miami started the 2026-27 season with four straight losses but has since found a groove, carrying a 7-6 record and a four-game win streak into Monday night's game against the Houston Rockets (11-3). Adebayo said the team's slow start wasn't a surprise after the integration of so many new faces, led by two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo.

"We're starting to figure stuff out, but we still got a long way to go," he said. "Obviously, it's a new team, everybody's still trying to adjust to one another, figure out how to mesh the way we play together, and how we try to get a flow as much as possible throughout the game to where it's consistent."

Adebayo's new partnership with Antetokounmpo has been rocky at times, and the big man's numbers have dropped slightly while trying to adjust to his new running mate. Legends like former Heat star Udonis Haslem and Hall of Famer Kevin Garnett have recently called out Adebayo for his play this season, but the 29-year-old knows they simply want to bring the best out of him.

"Speaking on UD, that's somebody I talk to every day. So it's not like it's a shot at me, but it's like I'm hearing a familiar voice, as always. So he's doing that because he cares," he said. "For KG, he was a role model of mine. I looked up to KG. So to hear somebody that I looked up to set a certain expectation and a standard for me, you look at it as he sees your potential."

In addition to learning Antetokounmpo on the court, Adebayo said he's still adjusting to not seeing him as an opponent.

"For me, it was getting used to being around him because we've always competed against each other. So every time I saw him, it was more like I'm in competition mode; I'm intense, ready to compete," Adebayo said. "And now I got to get used to just seeing him, like I'm going to my treatment time, and I see him. Like, you still got to adjust. But the most part is just getting to know him. That's really what it is."

He added: "I'm still getting used to how much he talks. Not saying he's just a Chatty Cathy, but to just have a conversation with him. He's very vocal, and then obviously we get on the court and behind the scenes when we're watching film, he's very vocal in those settings."

Antetokounmpo's arrival has surely raised expectations in Miami, and Adebayo isn't shying away from championship expectations. However, he's not getting ahead of himself, and he wants the Heat's identity to be a hard-nosed defensive team, which would help everything else fall into place.

"I think for us to be successful, I want us to be a top-three defense in this league, because it leads to all our strengths," he said. "Giannis in transition, Davion [Mitchell] in transition. Obviously, people are trying to find Klay [Thompson] in transition. Everybody's playing downhill, and that causes havoc for other teams."

articles.title: JJ Redick Calls Out Lakers' Struggles Despite Luka Doncic, LA's 12-2 Record After Win vs. Suns
articles.summary: Despite improving to 12-2 with Sunday's 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick isn't happy with his team.
articles.body:
Despite improving to 12-2 with Sunday's 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick isn't happy with his team.

Per The Athletic's Law Murray , Reddick called out the Lakers for their defensive lapses, particularly late in games.

"I told the team this after the game — we're working too hard, and we're playing too hard, to build these leads — it's a disservice to each other to take your foot off the gas," Redick said after the Lakers were outscored 43-27 in the fourth quarter. "I thought defensively, (we) did a lot of really good things through three quarters. Going to the fourth, we got a 107 defensive rating, and then we have a 165 defensive rating in the fourth. I believe we can be a good defensive team. This has been consistent now — this is a trend. Gotta be better in the fourth quarter."

Lakers star guard Luka Doncic put on another scintillating performance with 43 points and nine assists to lead Los Angeles to its eighth straight win.

While the Lakers are now tied for the best record in the Western Conference, Redick is right to point out that the way his team is playing is untenable. Los Angeles has given up over 100 points in nine of its last 10 games, including in every game during this current win streak.

The Lakers won't be able to rely on simply putting up big offensive numbers every night, especially when things get tighter in the playoffs. Los Angeles will have to find consistency on defense if it hopes to compete for an NBA title this year.

The Lakers will try to follow Redick's direction as they seek their ninth straight win on Tuesday against the Charlotte Hornets (4-9).

articles.title: New NBA Trade Rumors on Trey Murphy's Wild Asking Price from Pelicans amid Dejounte, Zion Buzz
articles.summary: New Orleans Pelicans small forward Trey Murphy III has been floated as a potential trade target ahead of the NBA's trade deadline in February, but teams may find it difficult to acquire him.
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans small forward Trey Murphy III has been floated as a potential trade target ahead of the NBA's trade deadline in February, but teams may find it difficult to acquire him.

During Monday's episode of the Hoop Collective, ESPN's Brian Windhorst and Tim MacMahon discussed how the Pelicans' asking price for Murphy may be preventing a trade.

"Trey Murphy has constantly been in trade rumors, but I've never actually heard anything about him ever actually getting close to getting traded," Windhorst noted.

MacMahon noted the Pelicans have never gotten close to trading Murphy because their asking price has been comparable to "first-born children."

"His minutes and scoring are down this year," Windhorst added. "He'll still have a lot of value, but maybe not the value that [the Pelicans] think."

NBA insider Marc Stein previously reported that the Pelicans have asked for three first-round picks in exchange for Murphy.

New Orleans seems reluctant to trade the 26-year-old despite underwhelming performances from its current core group of players. The Pelicans have just two playoff appearances in the past eight seasons and have won less than 30 games in each of the past two seasons.

MacMahon also reported that some people within the NBA are wondering if the Pelicans will trade two-time All-Star Zion Williamson after the team's 4-10 record to start the season.

Pelicans point guard Dejounte Murray is another player who could be on the move after requesting a trade last week. The team released a statement Friday saying they "will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization. released a statement.

Murphy will miss his fifth game on Monday due to patellar tendinopathy in both knees, but he has been a consistent starter while healthy. The sixth-year forward leads the team in minutes played (32.8) and ranks third on the team in points per game (15.6).

After the 2026-27 season, Murphy will have two years left on the four-year, $112,000,000 contract extension he signed in 2025, per Spotrac .

articles.title: Nets' Josh Minott, Bulls' Matas Buzelis fined $25,000 after making obscene gestures toward fans
articles.summary: Matas Buzelis' gesture was caught on the broadcast.
articles.body:
Brooklyn Nets forward Josh Minott and Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis were fined $25,000 by the NBA after making obscene gestures toward the fans the league announced Monday.

Minott's incident occurred at the end of the Nets' 129-110 road loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday.

Buzelis' occurred that same evening, and came with 11:19 left in the Bulls' 117-106 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves, per the NBA.

Buzelis' incident was caught on the broadcast. After hitting a free throw, the forward flipped off someone in the crowd.

Minott's obscene gesture occurred after the game ended, per the NBA's release. Video of his gesture wasn't immediately available.

Minott played just 1:46 minutes in the contest, going 0-for-1 from the floor. He was also responsible for a turnover.

The NBA did not announce additional details regarding Minott's gesture, though it may have come immediately after the game, when Minott threw up — and bricked — a final second 3-ball while down by 19.

Minott, 23, has seen his role reduced by a fair amount this season. After a midseason trade brought him to the Nets last season, Minott played in 16 games with the team, averaging 19.3 minutes a game.

In nine games this season, Minott is averaging just 6.7 minutes per contest.

articles.title: Women's basketball AP poll: South Carolina solidifies No. 1 ranking with win over USC as UConn stumbles again
articles.summary: South Carolina beat JuJu Watkins and USC on Sunday afternoon in a thrilling battle for the "Real SC" title.
articles.body:
South Carolina is the clear No. 1 team in the country. Sunday afternoon's win over JuJu Watkins and USC proved that.

The Gamecocks beat Watkins and the Trojans in a thrilling battle for the "Real SC" title in South Carolina for yet another ranked win already this season. The Gamecocks, who also beat Maryland and North Carolina in the opening week of the season, held onto their No. 1 ranking in the latest Associated Press poll that was released on Monday.

Tessa Johnson dropped a career-high 28 points in the win on Sunday, and Joyce Edwards had a double-double with 20 points and 10 rebounds. And while they lost, Watkins and the Trojans were right there until the end. Watkins had 25 points in the outing, and the Trojans cut the lead to just a single possession in the final minute.

The loss only moved USC down one spot to No. 4 in this week's poll. Michigan remained at No. 2, Louisville jumped to No. 3 and Duke held at No. 5.

The big question this week, though, has to do with Geno Auriemma's UConn group in Storrs. The Huskies looked bad on Sunday afternoon in their matchup with Louisville . The Cardinals rolled to an 18-point win behind a 21-point outing from Imani Berry, which kept them a perfect 6-0 on the season. That moved them up to four spots into the top five. UConn shot just 34% from the field in the loss, and had four total bench points. The Huskies now sit at No. 7.

The loss was UConn's second already this season after an 11-point loss at Michigan in the opening week. While two losses shouldn't derail a season, things won't get any easier for UConn in its non-conference slate . The Huskies will go up against top-ranked South Carolina, No. 5 Duke, No. 18 Maryland, No. 13 Notre Dame, Tennessee and No. 9 LSU all before Big East play gets going. That's a brutal slate, one that may end up hurting them come NCAA tournament seeding time if Auriemma isn't able to right the ship.

While it's hard to count him out, considering the dominant run he's been on since taking over at UConn, this season hasn't gotten off to the best start for Auriemma.

articles.title: Detenido en Nigeria un jugador de baloncesto con 34 kilos de cannabis
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense Greene Da'monte Khiree, de 28 años, dice ser profesional en Tailandia
articles.summary: El estadounidense Greene Da'monte Khiree, de 28 años, dice ser profesional en Tailandia
articles.body: Las autoridades nigerianas detuvieron en el Aeropuerto Internacional Murtala Muhammed de Lagos (suroeste) a un estadounidense de 28 años que asegura ser jugador profesional de baloncesto en Tailandia por intentar introducir casi 34 kilos de cannabis, informó la Agencia Nacional Antidrogas de Nigeria (NDLEA, en inglés). El detenido, identificado como Greene Da'monte Khiree y natural de Savannah, en el estado estadounidense de Georgia, llegó el pasado 11 de noviembre a Lagos en un vuelo de Emirates procedente de Tailandia con escala en Dubái, según un comunicado de la NDLEA que recogen este lunes medios locales. Los agentes de la NDLEA sometieron al sospechoso a vigilancia tras recibir información de inteligencia y observaron que abandonó sus dos maletas facturadas antes de intentar salir del aeropuerto únicamente con su equipaje de mano. Los agentes lo detuvieron posteriormente en el aparcamiento del aeropuerto y registraron las dos maletas abandonadas, que llevaban etiquetas con su nombre. En su interior encontraron 32 paquetes con un total de 33,95 kilos de 'Loud', una potente variedad de cannabis. Khiree afirmó durante el interrogatorio que vive en Tailandia desde octubre de 2025, donde asegura jugar profesionalmente al baloncesto, y que había viajado a Nigeria de vacaciones para establecer contactos relacionados con su carrera deportiva. Sin embargo, la NDLEA señaló que un examen forense de su teléfono móvil encontró información que apunta a que conocía y estaba implicado en la operación de narcotráfico. La detención formó parte de una serie de operaciones anunciadas este domingo por la agencia antidrogas nigeriana en diferentes puntos del país. Ese mismo 11 de noviembre, también en el aeropuerto de Lagos, los agentes interceptaron 25,05 kilos de metanfetamina ocultos en paquetes de cereales que llegaron de Sudáfrica y detuvieron a un ciudadano nigeriano de 56 años. La NDLEA ha intensificado en los últimos meses sus operaciones contra redes nacionales e internacionales de narcotráfico, incluidas investigaciones sobre laboratorios clandestinos de metanfetamina en el país. El pasado septiembre, las autoridades nigerianas anunciaron la detención del mexicano Arturo Carrera Loaiza, al que vincularon con una red de laboratorios clandestinos de metanfetamina, dentro de una investigación que también llevó al arresto de otros ciudadanos mexicanos y nigerianos.

images.caption: Greene Da'monte Khiree, con los 34 kilos de cannabis que le fueron incautados.

articles.title: 2026-27 NBA News, Injury Updates Nov. 16: Stephen Curry injured, Dejounte Murray makes trade request
articles.summary: Maybe one of these weeks I can write a summary that doesn't start with critical injuries.
articles.body:
Welcome to our weekly Monday Morning NBA notebook, a quick hit of NBA news and injuries from around the league to catch you up on what happened in the past week. Maybe one of these weeks I can write a summary that doesn't start with critical injuries.

The Golden State Warriors have been one of the great stories of the young season, with rookie Yaxel Landeborg grabbing headlines and winning games. The Warriors have beaten the Lakers, Timberwolves and Nuggets at points this season.

But this was still Stephen Curry's team, and his throwback start — 27.8 points per game, shooting 45.3% from 3-point range — is the foundation of all that winning. Now he is out with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in a couple of weeks, but reportedly could miss more like a month. In the game where he got injured and the game he missed so far, the Warriors got blown out. It might be a rough few weeks coming up in the Bay Area.

Caleb Wilson hasn't been the best rookie out of this class so far this young season, but he's been the most entertaining, averaging 18.9 points and 6.2 rebounds a game. More importantly, he gives the Bulls and their fans a real direction for the future after too many years of mediocrity (at best).

Now he is out 4-6 weeks with a hand fracture. Which just takes the air out of the sails in Chicago. It shouldn't impact winning or (more often) losing, they have been about the same with him on or off the court this season, but he brought a joy to the Bulls that is going to be missing for a bit.

We have our first trade request of the season : Dejounte Murray's agent (Rich Paul of Klutch Sports) told the New Orleans Pelicans Murray wants to be moved, something the Pelicans came out and confirmed.

When the Pelicans traded for Murray in the summer of 2024 it seemed like a good move on paper, he was the kind of guard who could bring together a talented roster that wasn't quite fitting with Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III and others. It didn't work out that way, as he ruptured his Achilles that first season in New Orleans and missed the majority of his first two seasons there.

Jeremiah Fears is the point guard of the future in New Orleans, and he and Murray do not mesh well as a backcourt. This is best for everyone. That said, after injuries and a couple of down years because of it, the market for Murray is not going to bring a big return, so don't be surprised if this drags out into 2027 and closer to the February trade deadline.

The NBA is going to take its talents to South Beach.

The 2028 NBA All-Star Game will be in Miami, the first time the NBA's midseason showcase has been in the city since 1990 (Magic Johnson was your MVP that year). Miami has everything the NBA wants in a venue — warm weather, plenty of hotel rooms for fans, and players love the city and aren't looking for an excuse not to attend/skip town early — but the game traditionally falls on Presidents Day weekend, which is also when the city hosts the massive Miami International Boat Show. That show took up hotel and convention space the NBA needed, but in 2028 the boat show is moving back a weekend, reports the Miami Herald. The NBA stepped into that gap.

This is a win for everybody — Miami was made for this game.

• Cooper Flagg making history. Flagg is having a "he has arrived" season — looking every bit a top 15 player in the world already — and this past week he made history: Flagg passed LeBron James to be the teenager with the most 40+ point games in league history, and he also passed Kobe Bryant and now has scored the second most points as a teenager. He turns 20 next month.

• Lauri Markkanen is out with a wrist injury. Utah has dropped 12 straight, and this isn't helping matters: He has a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will miss about a month (until mid-December). It likely means more touches for Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. • In the Jayson Tatum vs. Jaylen Brown showdown, Paul George was the star, reminding everyone he is still very good at basketball (and the Celtics got a convincing win). If he is healthy in April and May, the Celtics are a playoff threat in the East.

• The Bulls' Matas Buzelis and the Nets Josh Minott each have been fined $25,000 by the league for "making an obscene gesture towards the spectator stands." As a rule, the NBA frowns on players flipping off paying customers.

• Sacramento added veteran center Mason Plumlee to the roster. The Kings have a lot of centers on the roster, but that's not working as planned: Domantas Sabonis starts but is slumping, the future at the five may be Maxime Raynaud but he is injured, then there is Dylan Cardwell and, for small-ball lineups, Precious Achiuwa. Plumlee is not going to see a ton of minutes but the Kings could use the mentor.
